news.headline: NPR investigation: mall skincare stores sold $19.50 creams for $1,300
news.summary: NPR's Oct 14 investigation into Mazal Group (Voupre, Orogold, Vine Vera, Lionesse…): free-sample mall stores pressured older and disabled shoppers into charges from hundreds of dollars to $100K+; one product NPR lab-tested had no detectable vitamin A or E despite the label; a Hawaii class action settled in June 2026 and the company dropped its California license in September.
news.her_angle: De-influence: what a $1,300 'anti-aging rescue solution' can't do that a $12 drugstore retinol does.

news.headline: First new US sunscreen filter in 25 years is now on store shelves
news.summary: AP (Oct 14): bemotrizinol (BEMT) sunscreens — Neutrogena Ultra Sheer SPF 70 pictured — are arriving in US stores; the FDA cleared the filter in June and Neutrogena's Sep 17 release put it on Amazon first with nationwide retail 'in October'. The in-store arrival is the new part; the approval is background.
news.her_angle: Shelf review: what BEMT actually adds (UVA, photostability) — and why your mineral SPF isn't obsolete.

news.headline: Harvard study: 1 in 3 online 'eczema' creams hid a superpotent steroid
news.summary: JAMA Network Open (Oct 8, 2026; Harvard Medical School authors; doi 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.38654): 6 of 18 OTC skin products sold online for eczema and persistent rashes — Neoprosone, Zudaifu, Qian Nian Qi Cao — contained undeclared clobetasol propionate. Covered by Medscape and Dermatology Times; no tracked creator is on it. At the 7-day edge of the window.
news.her_angle: The 'herbal' eczema cream that clears you overnight is probably a prescription steroid — the rebound and the thinning that follow.
